children: Indonesia has raised the amount of diesel allocated to its subsidy programme in 2027, while keeping its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) allocation unchanged, the energy ministry said on Monday in a parliamentary hearing.
Indonesia will allocate 19 million kilolitres of subsidised diesel in 2027, about 2% higher than this year's allocation of 18.64 million kilolitres.

Energy ministry senior official Laode Sulaeman said at a separate meeting that subsidised diesel consumption this year is expected to reach 20.27 million kilolitres, exceeding the original allocation.
Indonesia has implemented a 50-50 blend of palm-based diesel and conventional diesel, known as B50 since the second half of this year in an effort to reduce its dependency on imported fuels.
The subsidised LPG allocation for next year is set at 8 million metric tons, unchanged from this year, but lower than the 8.67 million tons expected to be consumed this year.
Indonesia's oil lifting target has been set at 612,500 barrels of oil per day and 954,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day for 2027.
